title: Early Austin Paving and Police Plans
summary:
• **Road Infrastructure Push**: Council approved major spending on Congress Avenue paving ($500), a retaining wall project ($3,500), and equipment including a rock crusher to improve street conditions throughout the city.

• **Public Space Reclamation**: Officials ordered the Marshal to open up blocked passages and remove the Alliance Cotton Yard from public property near Block 190, clearing the area for pedestrians and vehicles while addressing "undesirable persons" living there.

• **Auto Regulation and Safety**: Council passed a new ordinance prohibiting people from interfering with automobiles without the owner's permission, plus ordered the removal of an overloaded and dangerous utility pole at Sabine and East 11th streets.

• **Street Maintenance Staffing**: Council authorized hiring six teamsters at $45/month and one equipment operator at $50/month to support the city's street work and new rock crushing plant.

• **Railroad Obstruction Dispute**: Council agreed to join a lawsuit against the International and Great Northern Railroad to force them to clear obstructions from property that should be part of Third Street.

Austin, Texas, April 6th,1908 .
To the Honorable the City Council of the City of Austin. Gentlemen:

**Special on Rock Crusher**

Your Special Committee appointed to test the working of the rock crusher offered for sale
by the County Commissioners of Hays County, beg to report that we made the trip to San
Marcos and saw the crusher satisfactorily break up several tons of rock. We therefore
recommend that the crusher,elevator and screen be shipped to Austin. The same have been
received here, and are being put in shape to crush rock. Approval of our action,and
authorization of the purchase at $ 250.00 are respectfully recommended:

F M Maddox
W C Reid
P G S Iredell
